paper.title_en: Magnetic-field-free parity-protected qubit based on a narrow altermagnet Josephson junction
paper.abstract_en: Altermagnets provide a new route to engineer superconducting circuits without magnetic fields. We theoretically study the Andreev bound state (ABS) spectrum of a finite-width altermagnet-based Josephson junction and show how the <math><mi>d</mi></math>-wave altermagnetic symmetry and geometric confinement shape its low-energy excitations. We find a clear distinction between the two <math><mi>d</mi></math>-wave symmetries: <math><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub></math> order produces spin splitting, whereas <math><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub></math> order preserves spin degeneracy and exhibits splitting of the ABS spectrum induced by intermode hybridization. Leveraging these novel features, we propose applying a transverse electric field to tune the system and realize a magnetic-field-free, parity-protected superconducting qubit that we call altermon.
